note: Structured 'Weld Diagnosis' content from the Welding Tips section. Each defect lists the manual's exact possible-causes-and-solutions, tagged with which processes each cause actually applies to (the manual marks some MIG-only causes explicitly; that tagging is preserved here so answers don't recommend a gas-flow fix to a gasless Flux-Cored user).

wireWeld.note: Applies to MIG (solid core, gas-shielded) and Flux-Cored (gasless) wire welding.

defects.name: Porosity
defects.description: Small cavities or holes in the bead.

causes.solution: Check that polarity is set correctly for the type of welding.
Increase flow of gas. Clean nozzle. Maintain proper CTWD (contact-tip-to-work distance).
causes.note: MIG only — Flux-Cored (gasless) does not use external shielding gas, so this cause does not apply to Flux-Cored porosity.

causes.solution: Use shielding gas recommended by the wire supplier.
Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain wire is clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
Maintain steady travel speed.
Reduce contact-tip-to-work distance.

defects.name: Burn-Through
defects.description: Base material melts away, leaving a hole in the weld.

causes.solution: Reduce current and/or wire feed speed.
Increase travel speed and ensure it is kept steady.
Reduce wire feed speed.
Use two hands or rest hand on a steady surface.
Maintain steady travel speed.
Reduce CTWD.

defects.name: Excessive Spatter
defects.description: Fine spatter is normal. Spatter that is grainy and large is a problem.

causes.solution: Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain wire is clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
Check that polarity is set correctly for the type of welding.
Increase flow of gas. Clean nozzle. Maintain proper CTWD.
Reduce wire feed speed.
Reduce CTWD.

defects.description: Small cavities or holes in the bead.

causes.solution: Clean workpiece down to bare metal. Make certain fill material and Electrode are clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
Maintain steady weld speed.
Use two hands or rest hand on a steady surface.
Maintain steady weld speed.

defects.name: Coat of Slag Over Weld
defects.description: Slag is a necessary part of a stick weld — it shields the weld from impurities while cooling. Not a defect by itself.

causes.solution: Clean off the slag with a Chipping Hammer and Wire Brush after welding.

stickPenetration.note: Workpiece heat control / weld penetration diagnosis for Stick welding.

categories.name: Excess Penetration / Burn-Through
categories.description: Weld droops on top and underneath, or falls through entirely, making a hole. Not hot enough → too hot.

causes.solution: Reduce current.
Increase welding speed and ensure it is kept steady.

categories.generalFix: To reduce workpiece heat and limit penetration (for thinner workpieces): decrease current, weld more quickly.

categories.name: Proper Penetration
categories.description: Weld is visible underneath and bulges slightly on top. This is the target result.

categories.name: Inadequate Penetration
categories.description: Weld does not contact the joint fully, just on the surface.

causes.solution: Keep arc on leading edge of weld puddle; hold torch at proper angles.
Slow down so fill material has time to melt into the weld location; increase current.
Bevel thick workpieces, allow a slight gap, and weld in several passes.
Increase amount of fill material.

categories.generalFix: To increase workpiece heat and penetration (for thicker workpieces): increase current, weld more slowly.
